head:
Executive Orber.
The Executive order made by President Roosevelt of date March 30,
1905: recites as follows:
With the view that hereafter under no circumstances whatever
shall any unclassified laborer lbe assigned to classified work, I direct
that the additional laborers referred to as shown in reports already
made to the Civil Service Commission be regarded as classified in the
positions occupied by them on the date of this order, and that they
may he promoted to the clerical grade or transferred in the manner
proi~ided by the civil-service rules and regulations.
It appears that in certain cases the work of various Departments,
independent offices and bureaus is of such character that it cannot be
economically and conveniently done consistently with a rigorous adher-
ence to the division between classified and unclassified work. In such
cases unclassified laborers are engaged for the greater part of their time on
unclassified work, but at the same time there is certain classified work
which could be more economically and conveniently done if such laborers
wverc permitted to do it incidentally, and not as a part of their main work
or employment.
It is therefore ordered that hereafter where such a state of things
exists as is above recited unclassified laborers may be assigned to classified
work incidentally, but not as a part of their main work, in cases where
such work cannot be conveniently and economically done by classified
employees, but never without the prior consent o

machine_read.last_words: public scandal by their activiity WM TAFT THE WHITE HOUSE Imail No

Executive Orber
Whenever in the opinion of the Secretary of the Navy a strict enforce-
ment of the provisions of section T, Rule I of the civil service rules would
influence the result of a local election the issue of which materially affects
the local welfare of the Government employees in the vicinity of any navy
yard or station, the Civil Service Commission may, on recommendation of
the Secretary of the Navy, and after such investigation as it may deem
necessary, permit the active participation of the employees of the yard or
station in such local election. In the exercise of the privilege which may
be conferred hereunder, persons affected must not neglect their official
duties nor cause public scandal by their activiity,
WM H TAFT
THE WHITE HOUSE,
Imail 14, 1909.
[No. 1072.1

civil officers with whom she has had temporary employment, may be
appointed to a clerkship in the classified service without examination for
the reason that her husband, Frank Del. Carrington, late Major First
U. S. Infantry, was unjustly convicted in the civil courts of the Philippines
of certain criminal charges, as now decided by the Supreme Court, and this

head:
Executive Orber.
It is hereby ordered that the following tracts of public land near
Sparta, Wisconsin, be reserved from sale and set apart for military pur-
poses in connection with a target range, as authorized by an Act of Con-
gress approved March 4, 1909 (Public-- No. 328, p. 65), viz:
The northeast quarter of the northwest quarter, section four; the
southwest quarter of the northwest quarter, section six; the northeast
quarter of the northeast quarter, section 8; all in township seventeen
north, range two west, fourth principal meridian. Also the northwest
quarter of the northeast quarter, the southeast quarter, and the south
half of the southwest quarter, section two; the northeast quarter of
the northeast quarter, section ten ; and the southeast quarter of the
northwest quarter, section twelve; all in township seventeen north,
range three west, fourth principal meridian.
WM H TAFT
THE WWVITE HOUSE,
May 21, 1909.
[No. 1075.1
